Public data. Built from nflverse (nflfastR play-by-play, NGS participation, FTN charting), mapped onto the PFF GamePBP layout. Run concepts, PFF success codes, yards after contact and receiver alignment are not in this source; see What nflverse cannot cover at the end.

Sample: 8 games (Sep 13, 2026 to Nov 08, 2026) · 515 offensive plays · Opponents: ARZ, DAL, HST, LA, NO, PHI, TEN, WAS
Source: NYG_2026_nflverse_GamePBP.csv · Generated Nov 10, 2026 18:07 · Success = standard yardage definition · EPA = nflfastR model

Key findings

Tendencies

  • Passes on 58% of all plays and 51% of neutral early-down plays (1st/2nd down, outside 2-minute drills).
  • QB alignment is a strong run/pass key: under center they run 71% of the time (n=192); in shotgun they pass 80% (n=306).
  • Pistol is a real part of the menu: 17 plays, 6% pass.
  • Tell: 3rd Down + Medium (4-6) -> pass 100% of the time (n=20, 95% lower bound 84%).
  • Tell: 3rd Down + Long (7-10) -> pass 95% of the time (n=37, 95% lower bound 82%).
  • Tell: 3rd Down + Extra Long (11+) -> pass 96% of the time (n=26, 95% lower bound 81%).
  • Tell: Shotgun + 3rd Down -> pass 85% of the time (n=101, 95% lower bound 77%).
  • Run game is built on Middle and Left Guard: 45% of carries.
  • Predictability: knowing personnel, alignment, down and distance lifts a defense’s run/pass guess from 58% to 79% (leave-one-out).

Strengths

  • Most efficient run gap: Left End, +0.10 EPA/carry, 5.1 YPC, 56% success (n=27).
  • Primary target: M. Nabers (#1) (WR), 30% target share, 53 catches for 648 yards, +0.23 EPA/target, 29 first downs.
  • Most efficient receiver: T. Tracy Jr. (#29) (HB), +0.64 EPA/target on 7 targets, aDOT 0.6, 10.8 YAC/rec.
  • Lead back C. Skattebo (#44): 46% of carries, 4.3 YPC, 46% success. Favorite gap: Middle.
  • Most total value: M. Nabers (#1), 18.1 total EPA on 78 touches + targets (648 scrimmage yards).
  • Deep shots (20+ air yards): 16% of targets, 39% complete, +0.59 EPA/target (n=41).

Vulnerabilities

  • Play action: 21% of dropbacks, -0.05 EPA/play vs +0.12 without (n=63 vs 238).
  • Least efficient run gap: Right Tackle, -0.56 EPA/carry, stuffed (0 or fewer yards) on 31% (n=16).
  • On 3rd and Extra Long (11+) they convert only 23% (n=26); they pass 96% of the time there. Overall 3rd-down conversion: 42%.

n = the number of plays (or carries / targets) behind a number, i.e. the sample size. Findings are generated by fixed rules (see Methodology) and include sample sizes. Treat any rate built on fewer than 10 plays as anecdotal.

8. Pre-snap tells and predictability

Always guessing the more common play type is right 58% of the time. Using personnel, alignment, down and distance bucket (leave-one-out cell rates) is right 79% of the time, a lift of 21%.

Methodology and data notes

How the sample was built
Step Plays
Offensive snaps in file 579
Run or pass plays (drops penalties / no-plays) 527
Downs 1-4 (drops PATs / 2-pt tries) 527
Excluding garbage time 527
Excluding QB kneels and spikes 515

What nflverse cannot cover (or only approximates)

  • Personnel / formation / coverage / routes: nflverse participation data covers only 0% of these plays (it is typically posted after the season), so those sections are mostly empty.
  • Run concepts: nflverse has no blocking-scheme charting (inside zone, duo, power …). Section 4 groups runs by gap and direction instead (e.g. ‘Left Tackle’, ‘Middle’).
  • PFF success codes (pff_OFFSUCCESS): not in nflverse. Success uses the standard 40/60/100 yardage rule only.
  • EPA / EP: nflfastR’s public model, not PFF’s. Values are close in spirit but not identical.
  • Yards after contact: not in nflverse, so the before/after-contact split for rushers is unavailable (yards per carry is shown instead).
  • Receiver alignment (slot / wide / backfield): not in nflverse. ‘Main align’ is blank.
  • Personnel is counted from the roster positions of the 11 players on the field (RB+FB, TE). A WR listed as TE on the roster counts as a TE. ’(*)’ = 6+ offensive linemen.
  • Garbage time is approximated with win probability (second half, pre-snap WP below 0.01% or above 99.99%). Calibrated against a licensed PFF sample.
  • 2-minute flag: inside the final 2:00 of either half (PFF’s 4-minute flag has no equivalent).
  • Pressure is NGS ‘was_pressure’ (yes/no); time to pressure is not available.

Column names below refer to the PFF GamePBP layout the nflverse data was mapped onto.

  • Pass play / dropback: pff_RUNPASS = "P", which includes sacks and QB scrambles. Run: "R". Penalties and no-plays ("X") are removed.
  • QB alignment: Pistol if pff_PISTOL is set, otherwise Shotgun if pff_SHOTGUN is set, otherwise Under Center.
  • Success (standard): gaining at least 40% of the distance on 1st down, 60% on 2nd, and 100% on 3rd/4th, or earning a first down. PFF success codes are not in nflverse, so only the standard rule is used.
  • First down: pff_FIRSTDOWNGAINED = 1 or yards gained ≥ distance.
  • EPA: pff_EXPECTEDPOINTSADDED as provided. Passing EPA is attributed to the targeted receiver.
  • Target: a pass play with a recorded receiver, excluding sacks and scrambles. Receiving yards: yards gained on completions.
  • Explosive: runs of 10+ yards, passes of 20+ yards.
  • Field zone: ABSOLUTEYARDLINE is yards to the opponent’s end zone (so 1–20 is the red zone).
  • Tell: a pre-snap cue (personnel, alignment, down, distance, or combinations) with at least 10 plays where one play type reaches 80%. The 95% lower bound uses a Wilson interval.
  • Intervals: rates show 95% Wilson intervals; run-concept EPA shows ±1 standard error. With samples this small, most differences between groups are not statistically distinguishable; the report shows n everywhere so readers can judge.
  • Garbage time excluded: TRUE. 2-minute drills excluded: FALSE. **Personnel “(*)“** marks a jumbo package (an extra offensive lineman replaces a skill player); merged into the base grouping: FALSE.
